chunk_map.heading: Read the sharpen with a skeptical eye

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 9 "Next": line 99: "The quality criteria, the access-surface facts, and the hardening decision all feed into what M4 builds." — "the quality criteria" is never named anywhere earlier in this file (the m3-quality window is named at chunk 6 as a place to grab quotes, but no sentence in this file ever states what the quality lane produces or calls it "criteria"). Harm: a reader relying on this file alone can't tell which artifact "the quality criteria" points at, weakening the closing continuity claim into M4. Other referents in the same sentence (access-surface facts, hardening decision) DO resolve — hardening decision is named at chunk 3 ("pick one threat worth hardening against") and chunk 5 ("One hardening decision is enough"); access-surface facts traces to chunk 5's "The access surface is what STRIDE chews on." Only the quality-criteria phrase is ungrounded. Separately considered and cleared under the carve-outs: chunk 6 line 53's "the main quest window (*m3-security*)" and "m3-quality" window labels are never defined inside this file either, but the session-artifacts and module-arc-beats carve-outs cover them in spirit — the student reading this section just came out of the exercise that created those literal windows, so there's no real confusion, unlike the quality-criteria phrase which names an unestablished abstraction rather than a session object in front of the reader.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name what the quality lane produced earlier (e.g. in chunk 6) or swap "the quality criteria" here for the artifact it actually means (the test-strategy skill's conventions).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 2 "Prework": line 14: "**A feature you could ship in a few hours. Not a quarter-long epic.**" bolds a full two-sentence lead (12 words), not a ≲5-word handle. chunk 10 "Bring to Module 4": line 105: "**One scoped task you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit: a real slice. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**" bolds an entire multi-clause paragraph. Harm: rule 9 exists to keep bold reserved for scannable handles under projection; both spans are narrative sentences, not named terms, and read as shouted paragraphs on a wall-projected slide.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim each bolded span down to the handle phrase (e.g. bold only "a few hours, not a quarter-long epic" / "a real slice") and let the rest run as plain prose.
